item.title: Multiorbital driving of quantum geometric nonlinear transport in oxide interfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.28213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum geometry plays a relevant role in determining the intrinsic non-linear transport properties of low-dimensional electron systems. Here, we theoretically investigate the quantum geometric contribution to the non-linear conductivity in $\text{SrTiO}_3$-based two-dimensional electron gases, comparing the prototypical (001) and (111) crystallographic interface orientations. Using a multi-orbital tight-binding approach, we uncover the crucial role of the multiband electronic structure in determining the quantum-geometric contribution to nonlinear transport. In particular, we show how the hybridization of $t_{2g}$ orbitals near avoided band crossings shapes the momentum-space distribution of the band-normalized quantum metric and the resulting nonlinear conductivity. Furthermore, we reveal a strong dependence on crystal orientation: while the (001) interface exhibits sharp peak-and-dip features confined around Lifshitz transitions, the trigonal symmetry of the (111) interface promotes strong orbital mixing. Our results highlight how the interplay between orbital hybridization and crystallographic orientation gives rise to distinct quantum-geometric nonlinear transport responses in oxide interfaces.
item.dc:creator: Irene Gaiardoni, Mattia Trama, Roberta Citro, Annika Johansson

item.title: Wireless readout and control of cavity magnon-polaritons via photonic modes delocalised across a gap
item.description: arXiv:2611.28347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In cavity magnonics, photon-magnon hybridisation is typically detected by measuring the cavity response (i.e. measuring cavity resonance shifts through its reflection or transmission spectra). While a large body of work in the field has focused on three-dimensional cavities, a variety of two-dimensional resonators have also been explored as hosts for photonic modes due to their compatibility with on-chip integration. Nevertheless, the readout approach remains largely unchanged. Here, we demonstrate remote excitation and readout of cavity magnon-polaritons using two spatially separated, wirelessly coupled ring resonators. Through inductive coupling, energy is transferred between the resonators, enabling the magnonic system to be excited by one resonator while its hybrid-mode spectrum is detected through measurements of the other. We demonstrate wireless readout of cavity magnon-polaritons at separations ranging from millimetres to centimetres, identifying their characteristic response in the remotely measured spectrum. This establishes wireless resonator coupling as a route to remote interrogation of hybrid photon-magnon systems.
item.dc:creator: Alban Joseph, Ryan D McKenzie, Amy Eden, Morven Last, Shannon Howard, Alzbeta Oravcova, Mawgan A Smith, Robert L Stamps, Rair Macedo

item.title: Spherical HgTe nanocrystal: a multi-band effective mass study
item.description: arXiv:2611.28689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The size-quantized energies, eigenstates, and optical selection rules in a spherical HgTe nanocrystal are studied by solving the multi-band effective-mass equations analytically. The six-band Kane model, involving both the $\Gamma_{6}$ and $\Gamma_{8}$ bands within the spherical approximation, is employed in the derivation. The eigenstates can be classified by both the total angular momentum and the parity. As the nanocrystal radius varies, crossings occur not only between electron and hole energy levels but also among the hole levels themselves. The lowest two electron states (in each spin subspace) are surface states, one with even parity and the other with odd parity. The optical selection rules consist of two parts, namely, the parity selection and the angular momentum selection.
item.dc:creator: Rui Li

item.title: Quantum Hall Effect in a 3D Cross-Dimensional Quantum Anomalous Hall System
item.description: arXiv:2611.28751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We systematically investigate cross-dimensional transport and the resulting quantum Hall effect in 3D quantum anomalous Hall effect systems, which are constructed by coupling two Weyl-semimetal Hamiltonians. Our study unveils that the system hosts highly anisotropic surface states and chiral modes, leading to rich quantum Hall responses. Crucially, we clarify how magnetic fields applied along three high-symmetry directions dictate the evolution of the Chern numbers, chiral modes, and Hall responses. We discover that chiral modes along different directions can originate from distinct mechanisms, giving rise to various magnetic modulation characteristics. Furthermore, we unveil the breakdown of the conventional Chern-number-based bulk-boundary correspondence under magnetic fields, where the Chern numbers alone fail to fully characterize the evolution of the chiral states. This anomalous behavior is attributed to the unique momentum-space distributions of surface bands. These insights are further validated numerically through multi-terminal Hall transport simulations. Our findings expand the understanding of magnetic-field-driven mechanisms in 3D topological systems and provide deeper insights into the interplay between quantized Hall effects and Chern numbers in 3D systems.
item.dc:creator: Liang-Liang Cheng, Ao-Long Li, Zhi-Qiang Zhang, Hua Jiang

item.title: Local Pressure Induced Quantum Dot to Ring Transition and Aharonov Bohm Effect in Reconfigurable MoTe2 Bilayers
item.description: arXiv:2611.28786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that local pressure provides an effective means of engineering reconfigurable quantum confinement in MoTe2 homobilayers. By applying a smooth, spatially varying pressure profile, we show that the confinement geometry can be continuously tuned from a conventional quantum dot to a quantum ring, with the emergence of annular confinement being a distinctive feature of AB-stacked bilayers. This crossover originates from the pressure-induced spatial modulation in the electronic parameters, which produces an off-center minimum in the effective confinement potential, thereby redistributing the ground-state probability density away from the center and giving rise to an annular confinement geometry. In the quantum-ring regime, a perpendicular magnetic field gives rise to a flux-periodic energy spectrum and persistent currents, providing characteristic signatures of the Aharonov-Bohm effect. By coupling the pressure-induced quantum ring to source and drain leads, we further demonstrate pronounced Aharonov-Bohm conductance oscillations, accompanied by real-space current patterns exhibiting constructive and destructive interference at integer and half-integer magnetic flux quanta, respectively. These findings establish locally pressurized MoTe2 bilayers as a lithography-free platform for reconfigurable quantum confinement and realizing pressure-tunable Aharonov-Bohm interferometry in two dimensional materials.
item.dc:creator: Ibsal Assi, A. Belayadi, Hocine Bahlouli, Udo Schwingenschl\"ogl, J. P. F. LeBlanc

item.title: Floquet-Induced Valley Polarization and Topological Phases in Twisted Bilayer Graphene Heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2611.28797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically investigate twisted bilayer graphene (tTBG) heterostructures subjected to circularly polarized light. Inversion symmetry is broken through the combined application of an out-of-plane electric field and the incorporation of insulating substrates, enabling precise control of the valley degrees of freedom and associated topological phases. We identify a regime in which the valley degeneracy is lifted: one valley retains a gapless, linear Dirac-like dispersion, whereas the other develops a finite band gap and becomes electronically inactive. The interplay between Floquet driving and inversion-symmetry breaking induces topological phase transitions characterized by Chern numbers C = -2, C = -1, and C = 0, together with the emergence of perfectly valley-polarized domain-wall channels. Furthermore, magnetic asymmetry arising from proximity to adjacent two-dimensional ferromagnetic contacts enables spin-valley filtering. These findings establish the potential of graphene-based heterostructures as highly tunable systems for controlling spin and valley degrees of freedom.
item.dc:creator: A. Belayadi, I. A. Assi, A. Johansson, C. I. Osuala, H. Bahlouli, Udo Schwingenschl\"ogl, J. P. F. LeBlanc, A. Abbout

item.title: Interface invariants of rhombohedral graphene with layer-dependent potentials and couplings
item.description: arXiv:2611.29093v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Domain walls in the perpendicular bias of rhombohedral (ABC-stacked) graphene bind valley-resolved interface modes whose signed number is fixed by a bulk-difference invariant. We determine which values of this invariant are reachable when the layer potentials are arbitrary monotone profiles, as produced by screening, and when the interlayer couplings vary from bond to bond. Within the single-particle continuum model, the invariant of an $m$-layer stack equals the difference of occupied angular weights of the zero-momentum levels, which reduces the classification to the ordering of those levels. At equal coupling, nonlinear monotone potentials reproduce exactly the set of invariants of linear potentials, also under the requirement of a common energy gap: screening moves phase boundaries but creates no new invariant values. With bond-dependent coupling, we characterize all occupied configurations. The range of attainable invariants is unchanged, but the gaps inside it are filled, beginning at five layers. Reflection-symmetric stacks realize a large subfamily with a guaranteed common gap, and lower bounds on single-bulk gaps complete the set of invariants with a common global gap for five and six layers. Among the examples is an eight-layer domain wall defined purely by gates, whose number of co-propagating channels per valley switches from 8 to 16 as the gate strength increases. Exact transfer-matrix calculations of the interface spectrum reproduce every predicted signed crossing count. A norm bound gives the minimum spread of interlayer coupling compatible with a prescribed gap.
item.dc:creator: Yuelong Li

item.title: Population of spin orbit-split-electron branches in semimetallic HgTe quantum wells
item.description: arXiv:2611.29487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the results of experimental studies on magnetoresistance, the Hall effect, and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations performed in gated heterostructures with HgTe-based gapless semiconductor quantum wells. We show that in quantum wells with widths corresponding to a semimetallic charge carrier spectrum, electrons, in contrast to the idealized model, populate both spin-orbit-split branches of the spectrum. This occurs regardless of whether the Fermi level lies exclusively in the conduction band or within the conduction-valence band overlap region.
item.dc:creator: G. M. Minkov, O. E. Rut, A. A. Sherstobitov, A. V. Germanenko, S. A. Dvoretski, N. N. Mikhailov

item.title: FlakeForge: automated lithography-ready device layout from optical images of exfoliated van der Waals flakes
item.description: arXiv:2611.29509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fabricating a device from an exfoliated van der Waals flake requires finding a suitable flake under a microscope and designing its lithography layout by hand. We present FlakeForge, an open-source pipeline from raw optical images of a marker-patterned chip to a lithography-ready, multilayer design file. It scores flakes for device usability, aligns and scales each image from its markers, fits the user's device design to each selected flake's contour and connects every contact to a bond pad by a trace routed around all earlier devices, so no two overlap. Demonstrated on Hall bars and Little-Parks rings, it processed four chips in about half an hour, work that took an expert days. It runs fully unattended or pauses for user review. Adapting it to a new material, marker design or device dimensions requires only configuration, with no training data; a new device type requires only its geometry definition.
item.dc:creator: Or Berman, Ilay Mangel

item.title: Kinetic inductance of two-dimensional viscous electron fluid
item.description: arXiv:2611.29645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern high-mobility two-dimensional electron systems are pure enough to manifest hydrodynamic regime of electron transport similar to dynamics of classical fluids. With the bulk scattering controlled by momentum-conserving electron-electron collisions, these novel hydrodynamic materials demonstrate systematic violation of conventional metallic behavior due to the Drude model in stationary electric transport. In this letter, we study the linear reactive AC response of 2D electron fluid in a narrow channel geometry and show that the essentially non-local viscous dissipation induces non-trivial size effect in it. In particular, kinetic inductance, which represents collective inertia of the entire electron fluid, is enhanced by non-uniform flow profile and, in contrast to diffusive transport, dominates the electrical impedance already in collisional regime by virtue of viscous skin effect. The onset of reactive behavior falls within the microwave frequency domain in the state-of-the-art 2D hydrodynamic conductors which makes them promising material system for applications in high-frequency electronics at elevated temperatures.
item.dc:creator: A. A. Grigorev, A. N. Afanasiev

item.title: Sondheimer oscillations in Weyl semimetal films
item.description: arXiv:2611.29875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In conducting films subject to an out-of-plane magnetic field, electron motion between the surfaces gives rise to conductance oscillations periodic in magnetic field, known as Sondheimer oscillations. While this size effect has been investigated in conventional metals, its dependence on the Berry curvature of topological materials remains less explored. In this work, we extend the semiclassical Boltzmann description of Sondheimer oscillations to type-I Weyl semimetal films. We account for the Berry curvature, the orbital magnetic moment and the effect of the Zeeman coupling on the Fermi wavevector and the electronic group velocity. The Berry curvature and the orbital magnetic moment generate a beating pattern and chirping in the Sondheimer oscillations. In the thick-film and thin-film regimes, we provide analytical expressions for the longitudinal conductivity, which highlight the interplay between electronic band topology and boundary-scattering in magnetotransport.
item.dc:creator: Lucas M\'echet, Louis-Thomas Gendron, Ion Garate

item.title: Geometric Polarization-Virial Theorems for Field-Induced Dipolar Interactions and Force Reversal
item.description: arXiv:2611.30039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electric fields can turn attraction into repulsion between far-separated atoms, yet the complete angular mechanical structure governing this reversal has remained unknown. Here, we uncover an entropy-like geometric structure: the cubically weighted interaction free energy, r^3 F(r), is nondecreasing under physical dilation. This structure unifies two exact polarization-virial theorems for arbitrary stable quasistatic dipole assemblies and fully retarded dipole pairs under stated conditions. Consequently, the free energy has at most one zero and energetic cancellation precedes mechanical cancellation. A force zero retains strictly positive energy, whereas an energy zero retains an attractive force. The resulting analytical angular fine structure is resolved by a quantum harmonic oscillator pair, yielding the complete arbitrary-angle interaction energy and radial force that recover quantum-perturbative results. The conventional dipolar magic angle splits into strictly ordered energy- and force-zero angles; the latter uniquely bounds the radially repulsive sector and carries a positive energy barrier. Derived scaling laws and finite-sphere calculations provide experimentally testable signatures from microscopic dipoles to macroscopic polarizable bodies.
item.dc:creator: Shuze Zhu

item.title: Domain advantage in two-dimensional quantum-device design with multi-modal agentic harness
item.description: arXiv:2611.30043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-quality two-dimensional quantum devices are commonly fabricated from mechanically exfoliated crystals, whose irregular shapes and placement require a lithographic layout tailored to each specimen. Drawing these layouts remains largely manual. We introduce qlaybench, a benchmark that tests whether language-model agents can turn microscope images and experimental requirements into device layouts that fit the specimen. Agents with conventional tools often construct devices when material outlines are supplied, but struggle to identify those outlines from images. Modelled on the human workflow, qlaybot, a multimodal agentic harness, connects image interpretation to the tools used to align images, draw device features and inspect the resulting layout. We evaluate each layout with checks drawn from practical design experience, asking whether it fits the specimen and connects its intended components. With greater computational effort, an agent using qlaybot passes 81.5% of the benchmark tasks, compared with 24.1% when it uses conventional tools. This domain advantage highlights the importance of connecting scientific interpretation of a specimen to geometric design and provides a route towards reducing manual effort in two-dimensional quantum-device fabrication.
item.dc:creator: Shenhao Miao, Yizhou Li, Liqiao Xia, Ruihao Liu, Dingke Wang, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero, Eli Zeldov, Jiaqi Cai

item.title: A Unified Energy-Density Framework for Moir\'e Interface Energetics and Mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2611.30152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The mechanical response of moir\'e interfaces depends on how atomic registry combines with contact size and boundary geometry. An analytical description must retain this discrete lattice information while connecting microscopic interactions to the energetics of finite contacts. Here, we develop a unified energy-density framework for rigid van der Waals interfaces by expressing registry-dependent pair potentials and atomic densities in reciprocal space. The resulting formulation accommodates different lattice bases and atomic species, linking single-atom and molecular adsorption to infinite bilayers and finite crystalline contacts. Explicit expressions for circular and regular polygonal flakes separate the area contribution from boundary-dependent terms and connect microscopic corrugation coefficients to energy barriers, rotational torques, and interlayer shear stiffnesses. The boundary analysis recovers the quarter-power area scaling of the barrier envelope for circular flakes and distinguishes bounded oscillations from square-root area scaling for polygonal contacts according to edge orientation. A dimensionless criterion characterizes the polygon-to-circle crossover in terms of moir\'e wavelength, flake size, and side number. Direct-summation benchmarks support the finite-domain expressions, while calculations for two-dimensional ice on graphene demonstrate the corresponding boundary-scaling trends in a molecular lattice. Applications to interlayer shear and graphite compression connect the same microscopic interaction description to tangential and normal mechanical responses. The framework establishes an analytical connection between microscopic registry, moir\'e periodicity, and finite-domain geometry, providing a basis for understanding and tailoring the energetics and mechanics of van der Waals contacts.
item.dc:creator: Zhangke Lei, Weidong Yan, Zhicheng Feng, Wengen Ouyang

item.title: Quantum Geometry Effects in Lattice Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.30210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum geometric effects such as the Berry curvature and the quantum metric are well established in electronic transport, whereas in lattice dynamics the Berry curvature also plays a key role: adiabatically following the lattice, electrons generate a molecular Berry curvature that splits degenerate optical phonons into chiral partners. To determine how the quantum metric affects phonons, we go beyond adiabatic lattice dynamics, identifying Berry curvature and quantum metric contributions to the electronic response of the lattice. Using first-principles calculations in the magnetic topological semimetal EuB$_6$, we find that phonon modes with chiral splitting and those with nonchiral splitting coexist. Unlike the former, which originate from the Berry curvature, the latter arise from the pure quantum metric, while the Berry curvature contribution is forbidden by crystal symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Haoshu Li, Hao Chen, Qian Niu

item.title: Anatomy of orbital and spin responses in GaAs and Si: Hall, inverse Faraday, and magneto-optical Kerr effects
item.description: arXiv:2611.30297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magneto-optical signals in nonmagnetic semiconductors entangle spin and orbital contributions, both in angular-momentum generation and magneto-optical detection. We calculate these contributions for electron-doped GaAs and Si using density-functional theory, linear-response theory, and a second-order density-matrix treatment of the inverse Faraday effect. At small electron doping, the intrinsic orbital Hall conductivity exceeds its spin counterpart in magnitude, while the orbital contribution to light-induced magnetization dominates over broad photon-energy ranges. We show that orbital- and spin-resolved optical Hall and polar Kerr coefficients exhibit stronger sensitivity to orbital moments than to equal spin moments. This contrast reflects direct electric-dipole coupling to orbital motion versus spin-orbit-mediated coupling to spin polarization. Consequently, Si maintains a substantial orbital magneto-optical response despite its weak spin-orbit interaction. At probe energies of 1.5 eV in GaAs and 3.0 eV in Si, the magnitude of the Kerr rotation per unit orbital moment is approximately 5 and 13 times larger than that per unit spin moment, respectively. Combining the calculated Hall conductivities and Kerr coefficients with a phenomenological drift-diffusion model yields predominantly orbital edge signals for the assumed diffusion constants and relaxation lengths. These results indicate that optical detection of induced magnetization in doped semiconductors such as GaAs and Si can be dominated by orbital signals, and therefore cannot be interpreted solely in terms of spin polarization.
item.dc:creator: Sanaz Alikhah, Daegeun Jo, Peter M. Oppeneer

item.title: Edge-asymmetric magnetism in semi-Dirac quantum dots
item.description: arXiv:2611.30343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we investigated the electronic and magnetic properties of quantum dots (QDs) throughout the transition from the Dirac limit to the semi-Dirac limit and beyond. When non-interacting semi-Dirac fermions are confined in triangular QDs, the resulting electronic states near the Fermi level are localized asymmetrically among the three edges of these systems. In the presence of electron interactions, we show that these low-energy states favor the formation of edge-asymmetric magnetism in triangular QDs. In particular, the magnetic moments were localized only along a single edge of the zigzag triangular QDs, corresponding to an edge-asymmetric ferromagnetic ground state. For various system sizes, these zigzag triangular QDs exhibit a one-unit increase in the ground-state total spin ($\Delta S_z = +1$) beyond the semi-Dirac limit, revealing a striking result of this transition. In contrast, the remaining two edges are antiferromagnetically coupled in the armchair triangular QDs, indicating an edge-asymmetric antiferromagnetic (AFM) ground state. We further identified the AFM ground states in hexagonal QDs, indicating that these types of asymmetric configurations are not unique to triangular QDs. Collectively, edge-asymmetric magnetism could create potential opportunities for future spintronics.
item.dc:creator: Mustafa Polat

item.title: Scanning nanowire quantum dot with radio-frequency read-out
item.description: arXiv:2611.30427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scanning single-electron transistors (SETs) are highly sensitive local probes of charge and electric potential, but their integration with robust height control for scanning probe microscopy remains challenging. Furthermore, readout bandwidths are limited to tens of kHz, while characterizing faster charge dynamics is often of interest. Here, we present a scanning SET in the form of a nanowire (NW) quantum dot (QD) integrated at the apex of a non-contact atomic force microscopy (NC-AFM) cantilever. We demonstrate NC-AFM topographic imaging and local electrometry capability by mapping the electrostatic potential generated by a set of nanoscale voltage-biased gate electrodes. Comparison with electrostatic simulations shows agreement with the measured potential profiles. We demonstrate radio-frequency (rf) reflectometry read-out of the sensor, by embedding the QD in an LC-resonator. This platform establishes a route towards high-bandwidth scanning electrometry with simultaneous topographic contrast.
item.dc:creator: Aur\`ele Kamber, Luca Forrer, Valentina Zannier, Fabio Beltram, Lucia Sorba, Martino Poggio, Floris Braakman

item.title: All-in-one Spintronic Sensory Neurons for Magnetic Edge Intelligence
item.description: arXiv:2611.30740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic fields enable non-contact sensing through nonmagnetic materials, offering opportunities for magnetic edge intelligence in autonomous recognition, navigation, and control. However, directly converting magnetic stimuli into neural spikes for local neuromorphic processing remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate an all-in-one spintronic sensory neuron (SSN) based on spin-transfer-torque magnetic tunnel junctions (STT-MTJs) fabricated using a 40-nm magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM) process. By exploiting magnetic-field-modulated stochastic switching, the SSN enables probability-based sensing with an electrically tunable sensitive field window, allowing adaptive operation across different magnetic-field ranges without structural modification. This tunability alleviates the fixed sensitivity-range constraint of conventional tunneling magnetoresistance sensing, providing an accessible sensing range of +/-40 mT with an average probability sensitivity of 2.91%/mT. Importantly, the same stochastic switching process directly transduces magnetic stimuli into binary spike trains, integrating magnetic sensing, nonlinear rate encoding, and spike generation within a single nanoscale device. The resulting sigmoidal spike-rate response enables magnetic-field encoding, experimentally validated using the Neural Engineering Framework. Using experimentally characterized device responses, a simulated 10 x 10 SSN array achieves 90.7% accuracy in contactless magnetic-trajectory recognition with optimized encoding, approaching the software baseline. These results establish a scalable, MRAM-compatible approach to unifying programmable magnetic sensing and neural encoding for sensor-native edge intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Jiajia Jian, Bin Rong, Jiaxin Liu, Fangyi Zhao, Kai Li, Tao Huang, Xue Zhou, Xin Yue, Zeyu Ma, Xuefeng Zheng, Weidong Zhang, Jian Fu Zhang, Yumeng Yang, Zheng Chai

item.title: Two-dimensional Thyristor
item.description: arXiv:2611.30748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer a viable platform for next-generation electronics beyond sub-3 nm nodes, yet essential nonlinear circuit elements, such as thyristors, remain unexplored on atomically thin platforms. Here, we report an atomically thin reconfigurable electro-optical thyristor based on a lateral WSe2-MoSe2-WSe2-MoSe2 PNPN heterostructure, directly grown via sequential edge epitaxy. Unlike single-junction 2D diodes, this multijunction architecture exhibits thyristor-like nonlinear switching, including forward blocking, abrupt snapback, bistability, and electrical latching. The device exhibits a forward-blocking voltage of 183 V, corresponding to a critical electric field of 1 MV/cm. Under open-gate conditions, avalanche-assisted carrier multiplication and regenerative feedback are associated with a sharp forward-voltage drop of 175 V, a pronounced current surge, and an ultralow holding voltage. Gate-pulse modulation and temperature-dependent measurements indicate avalanche-assisted thyristor operation and latching behavior. This 2D lateral heterostructure enables a new route to nonlinear and bistable switching, latching, ultralow standby power, and adaptive logic, opening the way for reconfigurable 2D electronics and photonic integrated circuits.
item.dc:creator: Purbasha Ray, Rupali Verma, Biswajeet Nayak, Suman Kumar Chakraborty, Mayank Shrivastava, Prasana Kumar Sahoo

item.title: Aharonov-Bohm oscillations in transport through interacting quantum dots
item.description: arXiv:2611.30753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate electronic transport through a two-terminal Aharonov-Bohm interferometer with two quantum dots in the presence of finite intra-dot Coulomb interactions. With the help of a diagrammatic technique, we derive, within linear perturbation theory in the tunnelling-coupling strength, analytic expressions for the occupations, current, and interferometric visibility in terms of a coherence measure that involves the sum of four off-diagonal elements of the reduced density matrix. The latter are calculated numerically from a master equation for arbitrary settings of the system parameters. For some symmetric setups, we obtain closed-form expressions for the linear conductance. We systematically analyse the impact of a finite Coulomb interaction on the interferometric visibility, and reveal a rapid suppression of destructive interference upon breaking of system symmetries. Our results are supported by alternative methods, including the TraSPI method.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Oing, Alexander Hahn, J\"urgen K\"onig, Alfred Hucht

item.title: Interaction-driven ordering of multiple pseudospins and anomalous Hall metals in Bernal-stacked graphene
item.description: arXiv:2611.30906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent observations of anomalous Hall states in Bernal-stacked tetralayer graphene raise a fundamental question: How do electron-electron interactions organize multiple low-energy pseudospin sectors within each spin-valley flavor? Within the Hartree-Fock approximation, we analyze interaction-driven pseudospin ordering and spin-valley polarization as functions of displacement field and carrier density. We find a rich phase diagram shaped by the interplay between the two pseudospin doublets, including mixed flavor orders at charge neutrality and anomalous Hall metals upon doping. In particular, we identify topological states with $\sigma_{xy} \approx 6e^{2}/h$, consistent with recent experimental observations. Our results highlight the central role of multiple pseudospin doublets in the interaction-driven phases of even-layer Bernal multilayers.
item.dc:creator: Jeonghyeon Suh, Kyungjin Shin, Hongki Min

item.title: Molecular Pawns on a Surface Chessboard: Computational Investigation of Nanographenes with Atomistic Methods
item.description: arXiv:2611.30917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atomically precise nanographenes combine tunable electronic topology with localized, coherent spin states, making them candidate platforms for molecular quantum technologies. This review examines the multiscale theoretical framework governing these systems: the hierarchy of computational methods for describing magnetic properties, the substrate-molecule interface, on-surface synthetic kinetics, and supramolecular self-assembly. We highlight how density functional theory, automated reaction-path discovery, and spin-aware machine-learned interatomic potentials connect static electronic structure to mesoscale dynamics, and how magnetic exchange, optical excitations, and spin transport can be predicted before synthesis.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Lorenzo Mariano, Jacopo Lupi, Emilio Lorini, Matteo Briganti

item.title: Dirac-like bands and weak-field transverse transport in ABA trilayer graphene
item.description: arXiv:2611.30924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The low-energy electronic structure of ABA trilayer graphene is composed of light and heavy electron branches, which can be altered by an out-of-plane displacement field. Here, we show that, depending on the values of Slonczewski-Weiss-McClure parameters, a displacement field can inflict a band edge inversion, for which we identify the inversion conditions. This inversion is accompanied by a reversal of Berry curvature and giant topological magnetic moments at the band edges. In a weak perpendicular magnetic field, those topological magnetic moments produce valley splitting, giving rise to distinct anomalous transverse electrical and thermoelectric responses. These features offer a potential route to detecting the band inversion and constraining several of the least established tight-binding parameters, such as the on-site energy shift for the dimer pair of carbons $\Delta^\prime$ and the next neighbour hopping parameters $\gamma_2$ and $\gamma_5$.
item.dc:creator: Agustin Montemurro, Fujia Lu, Ellis R. Huntley, Vladimir Fal'ko

item.title: LeIFF: A localized-electron and ion force field for coupled nuclear and electronic dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.31029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical and machine-learned interatomic potentials enable large-scale simulations by replacing electronic structure with an effective energy surface for nuclear motion. This excludes electronic dynamics, electronic excitation and energy exchange between electrons and ions. First-principles electron dynamics can describe these processes, but its computational cost restricts system sizes and simulation times. Electron force fields offer an intermediate description by treating electrons as semiclassical dynamical particles interacting with ions. We introduce the localized-electron and ion force field (LeIFF), a compact physical model for both ground state bonding and excited electron dynamics. Valence electrons are represented by spin-labeled spherical charge distributions with dynamical centers and widths. The energy combines analytic electronic kinetic, Coulomb, and dispersion terms with spline-interpolated short-range interactions fitted to a large molecular data set. The resulting energy surface describes a variety of ground state properties across diverse bonding environments and charge states. It also provides a qualitative description of electronic behavior away from equilibrium. It shows improved robustness, accuracy, and transferability relative to earlier electron force-fields. Without any solid-state training, the same model describes dielectric screening and collective electronic response in silicon. LeIFF thus opens a route to large-scale simulations of nonadiabatic processes in molecules and solids, combining chemical bonding and nonequilibrium electronic motion within a common physical framework.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Mannino, Isidro Losada, Simon Divilov, Michelle Fritz, Younos Hashem, Ashraf Mrabet, Paula Mori S\'anchez, Javier Junquera, Mariv\'i Fern\'andez-Serra, Jose M. Soler

item.title: Protected Charge Readout Scheme Utilizing Nonlinear Resonators
item.description: arXiv:2611.31144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Charge detection of nanoscale quantum devices commonly relies on dissipative sensors, where signal absorption causes measurement backaction. Recently, nonlinear resonators showed a near-unity readout signal through an induced frequency shift. We show that this frequency shift protects the sensor, as it detunes the resonator from the measurement signal. The resonator excitation reduces while an enhanced readout signal is maintained. Our results, supported by numerical modeling, show that nonlinear resonators can combine strong readout contrast with reduced measurement-induced backaction.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Cicovic, Harald Havir, Pierre Glidic, Samuel Andersson, Sebastian Lehmann, Kimberly A. Dick, Claes Thelander, Ville F. Maisi

item.title: Cryogenic Luminescence Thermometry of Upconversion Micro- and Nanoparticles via Deep Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.28311v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Luminescence thermometry with single or optically trapped particles is hampered by weak signals that fluctuate with alignment, collection efficiency, and excitation conditions and, for $\mathrm{Er}^{3+}$-based probes, by the loss of sensitivity of the luminescence intensity ratio (LIR) at cryogenic temperatures. Here we use a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) to predict the temperature directly from single emission spectra of $\mathrm{NaYF}_4{:}\mathrm{Yb}^{3+},\mathrm{Er}^{3+}$ micro- and nanoparticles between $-150\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $105\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, and compare it with the standard LIR under adverse conditions deliberately reproduced with particle ensembles. From $-150\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $30\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, the 1D-CNN reduces the single-spectrum mean absolute error from $5.4\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $1.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and keeps its temperature uncertainty nearly constant down to the lowest temperatures, where Stark-component features remain temperature dependent while the LIR loses its sensitivity. Under deliberate optical misalignment, its error increases only from $0.58\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $0.88\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, whereas that of the LIR rises from $1.4\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $3.5\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The same approach reaches sub-degree accuracy ($0.21\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$) over a narrow temperature window and a single calibration valid across different pump powers and wavelengths. These results establish 1D-CNNs as robust single-shot thermometers and a step toward fast thermometry of single and trapped particles.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Jos\'e Coria Ledo, Lina W\"olcken, Lucas R. Mendicino, Santiago Gliosca, M. Claudia Marchi, Marcos Illescas, Beatriz Barja, Christian Tom\'as Schmiegelow

item.title: Coherent Control of Single-Photon Emission in Broadband Plasmonic Resonators
item.description: arXiv:2611.28493v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Encoding phase information with quantum emitters in metallic optical nanocavities is challenging due to ultrafast relaxation induced by the broadband nature of the plasmonic near field. Using macroscopic quantum electrodynamics theory, we demonstrate that an individual emitter strongly coupled to a plasmonic nanocavity field that is driven by a pulsed laser with frequency comb spectrum undergoes spontaneous emission of well-resolved one-photon pulses whose amplitude scales quadratically with the number of frequency comb components due to coherent accumulation, and ultrashort non-exponential temporal profiles with duration set by the light-matter coupling strength. Conditions are discussed for exponentially suppressing the probability of two or more emission events within the lifetime of the coupled emitter-nanocavity system. The spectral signatures of the optimal one-photon wavepackets are discussed. This work paves the way for the development of ultrafast laser-triggered single-photon emitters using atoms and molecules in optical nanocavities.
item.dc:creator: Athul S. Rema, Adri\'an E. Rubio L\'opez, Felipe Herrera

item.title: Systematically improvable semiclassical clustering for accurate and efficient quantum dynamics in large spin ensembles
item.description: arXiv:2611.28958v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Predicting the decoherence of spin qubits in realistic environments is key to identifying the interactions that limit their coherence---a prerequisite for designing better quantum technologies. While accurate methods for spin dynamics are limited to relatively small systems, the dissipative spin environments in real experiments typically involve orders of magnitude more spins. Semiclassical methods can reach these sizes, but their classical treatment of the bath cannot capture the sensor-bath entanglement that generates coherence revivals, especially under the application of refocusing pulses. Here, we resolve this tension. We introduce cluster spin-LSC, a method that clusters the sensor together with a few strongly coupled bath spins, treating them quantum mechanically in an otherwise classical spin bath. We show that our method is applicable to systems containing arbitrary spin species under dynamical decoupling pulse sequences. Our method converges systematically to the exact dynamics with cluster size, providing an internal consistency check when no exact benchmarks exist. We demonstrate that cluster spin-LSC recovers numerically exact coherence and population dynamics for a nitrogen-vacancy center and a molecular qubit, reducing day-long multi-GPU simulations to only minutes on a CPU. We further extend our method to systems with large spin baths that lie beyond the reach of exact methods. Our approach thus offers a scalable and systematically improvable route to accurately simulate the decoherence dynamics of sensors in realistic spin environments.
item.dc:creator: Pranay Venkatesh, Andr\'es Montoya-Castillo

item.title: Observation of nonadiabatic quantum tunneling in a driven correlated insulator
item.description: arXiv:2611.28980v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many emerging solid-state platforms for Floquet engineering, nonlinear transport, and high harmonic generation operate near the Keldysh crossover, where optical fields are sufficiently strong and fast to reshape electronic states on sub-cycle timescales. Despite its importance, the microscopic pathways for photocarrier generation in this regime remain poorly understood, as neither perturbative multiphoton absorption nor adiabatic tunneling provides an adequate description. Here, we perform time-resolved optical spectroscopy on the correlated van der Waals insulator NiPS$_3$ while systematically tuning the drive electric field and frequency over a wide range. In the crossover regime, we observe multiphoton-like resonances that are blue-shifted by ponderomotive effects within an otherwise tunneling-dominated absorption channel - a clear spectroscopic signature of adiabaticity breakdown. Hubbard-model simulations based on a time-dependent Gaussian variational approach qualitatively reproduce these features. Together, our results elucidate the microscopic mechanisms of charge excitation in the Keldysh crossover regime and identify a key ingredient for controlling strong-field nonlinear dynamics in correlated materials.
item.dc:creator: Mingyao Guo, Radu Andrei, Jaena Park, Je-Geun Park, Eugene Demler, David Hsieh

item.title: Scaling of phase rigidity without eigenstate coalescence
item.description: arXiv:2611.29463v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Phase rigidity vanishes as a power law near exceptional points, reflecting the coalescence of eigenstates at these points. In this Letter, we show that non-Hermitian skin effects induce distinct asymptotic behaviors of phase rigidity without eigenstate coalescence. To demonstrate this, we derive exact analytical results for three non-Hermitian chain models and verify them numerically. For the ordinary skin effect, phase rigidity decays exponentially with increasing system size $N$, as the right and left eigenstates are exponentially localized at opposite boundaries. For the scale-free skin effect, phase rigidity exhibits an $N^{-2}$ power-law approach to a nonzero constant as the right and left eigenstates have decay lengths proportional to $N$. For the algebraic skin effect studied here, phase rigidity can exhibit an $N^{-1/2}$ power-law decay to zero, with the right eigenstate algebraically localized near a boundary and the left eigenstate spread across the chain. These findings show that non-Hermitian skin effects govern phase-rigidity scaling by shaping the spatial profiles of the right and left eigenstates, enabling control of eigenstate nonorthogonality without exceptional points.
item.dc:creator: Shang-En Xie, Li-Mei Chen, Yao Zhou, Peng Ye

item.title: Apparent thermal conductivity governed by interface-injected phonon spectra
item.description: arXiv:2611.30276v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Thermoreflectance techniques such as time- and frequency-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR and FDTR) are widely used to measure the thermal conductivity of bulk materials, thin films, and interfaces. When phonon mean free paths $\Lambda_\omega$ become comparable to the thermal penetration depth, a Fourier analysis yields an apparent thermal conductivity $\kappa_{\rm app}$ that deviates from the bulk value $\kappa_{\rm bulk}$. Recent studies have highlighted the role of the phonon spectrum injected through the transducer interface, which is generally out of equilibrium owing to frequency-dependent transmission, and have shown that accounting for this nonequilibrium distribution can yield $\kappa_{\rm app}>\kappa_{\rm bulk}$, unlike conventional suppression-function analyses that predict only $\kappa_{\rm app}\leq\kappa_{\rm bulk}$. However, the spectral characteristics governing whether $\kappa_{\rm app}$ is enhanced or reduced remain unclear. Here, we resolve the surface-temperature response of semi-infinite Si mode by mode and show that short-$\Lambda_\omega$-weighted injection raises the surface temperature, whereas long-$\Lambda_\omega$-weighted injection lowers it. This behavior is governed by how deep the injected phonons travel before thermalizing with the lattice, which is set by their mean free paths, and by how effectively the substrate conducts the injected energy away, which is limited by its long-mean-free-path phonons. For an Al (70 nm)/Si structure, Fourier fits of synthetic TDTR phase signals give $\kappa_{\rm app}$ of Si from about 93 to 360 W/(m K) for different interfacial transmission spectra, and $\kappa_{\rm app}$ correlates with the heat-flux-weighted $\Lambda_\omega$ of the transmitted phonons. Thus, $\kappa_{\rm app}$ from thermoreflectance reflects not only the substrate thermal properties but also the phonon spectrum injected across the transducer interface.
item.dc:creator: D. G. Jeong, Terumasa Tadano, J. S. Lee

item.title: Spin-controlled thermophase and noise-optimized thermometry in multiorbital quantum dots
item.description: arXiv:2611.30315v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Converting temperature differences into electrical signals underlies both thermoelectric energy conversion and thermometry, which is essential for managing heat in cryogenic quantum technologies. Superconducting circuits typically show a weak thermoelectric response, since their quasiparticle spectrum is nearly particle-hole symmetric. In a Josephson junction, a temperature difference can instead be converted into a superconducting phase difference in an open circuit. We investigate this thermophase effect in a setup where the junction consists of a two-orbital quantum dot with Rashba spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and Zeeman splitting. A second orbital near the superconducting coherence peaks supports quasiparticle transport over a broad gate range. Zeeman splitting can enhance the thermophase by suppressing pair transport, while spin-orbit hybridization shifts the orbital resonances and can reverse the sign of the response. We assess the junction as a phase-based thermometer using a noise budget that includes readout and current noise together with fluctuations of the orbital energies and the magnetic field. The optimal operating points do not maximize the thermophase but balance a large quasiparticle response against sensitivity to parameter fluctuations. Under experimentally motivated noise assumptions, we obtain projected noise-equivalent temperatures of order $10\,\mu\mathrm{K}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ and determine the range over which a linear calibration remains accurate. Gate-tunable quantum-dot junctions thus offer a phase-based route to sensing temperature differences in superconducting circuits at sub-kelvin temperatures.
item.dc:creator: Markus Plautz, Jeroen Danon, Jacob Linder

item.title: Liouvillian Quasiparticle Spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2611.30441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quasiparticles play a central role in understanding closed quantum many-body systems, as they reduce complex many-body problems to effective single-particle descriptions and connect directly to spectroscopic measurements. In open quantum systems, the interplay between coherent dynamics and dissipation gives rise to unique phenomena, such as the Liouvillian skin effect and strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking. This raises a fundamental question: how can the quasiparticle picture be extended to open quantum systems to account for such phenomena and enable the experimental probing of quasiparticle spectra? Here we introduce coherent and incoherent Liouvillian quasiparticles, defined by responses to perturbations acting on one side and both sides of the density matrix, respectively. We propose spectroscopy protocols that couple the system to auxiliary levels, either coherently or via a dissipative pulse, to measure the corresponding complex quasiparticle energies. Numerical simulations of Liouvillians with skin effects validate these protocols, revealing nontrivial spectral winding associated with unidirectional transport in real space. Notably, coherent and incoherent quasiparticles can propagate in opposite directions within the same system. Furthermore, in models exhibiting weak and strong-to-weak $U(1)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking, our results unveil gapless Nambu-Goldstone modes in the coherent and incoherent quasiparticle spectra, respectively; the other quasiparticle spectrum remains gapped in each case. Our work provides a unified framework for theoretically describing and experimentally probing coherent and incoherent quasiparticles in open quantum many-body systems.
item.dc:creator: Kai Li, Masahito Ueda

item.title: Perfect Spin-to-Charge Signal Conversion via Inverse Spin Hall Effect in a Superconductor
item.description: arXiv:2611.30781v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spin-to-charge conversion is central to spintronics, but conventional spin Hall mechanisms are intrinsically limited by the small spin Hall angle. Here we show that superconductivity can overcome this limitation and enable near-unity spin-to-charge signal conversion. We consider a nonlocal spin-valve geometry in which a spin accumulation is injected into a superconductor and converted into a transverse charge signal through the inverse spin Hall effect. In the superconducting state, the strongly suppressed quasiparticle conductance below the gap allows the resulting charge imbalance to generate a voltage comparable to the injected spin bias, despite a small spin Hall angle. We derive the full nonequilibrium response including finite spectral broadening and finite temperature, and propose temperature and spin-bias-dependent measurements of the detector voltage to test our predictions.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo de las Heras, Ilya V. Tokatly, F. Sebastian Bergeret

item.title: Self-consistent Floquet theory of steady-state ordering in driven open systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.30996v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Periodically driven open systems have quasienergy bands whose steady-state occupations are set by the drive and reservoir. We formulate a self-consistent Floquet spectral theory of electronic ordering in the weak-reservoir-coupling limit, expressing the nonlinear mean-field equation and the particle-hole response in terms of quasienergies, steady-state occupations, and harmonic matrix elements that account for micromotion. We illustrate the theory in the square-lattice Hubbard model and show how the drive produces `dynamical nesting' conditions and how Floquet resonances produce \textit{hysteretic} responses due to multiple self-consistent solutions. Interestingly, we find that the hysteresis branches exhibit distinct Floquet topologies. Away from half-filling, we find that the combination of drive-induced detuning of the van Hove saddle points and the micromotion leads to the onset of switching between competing incommensurate orders.
item.dc:creator: Srinjoy Ghosh (IUB), Babak Seradjeh (IUB), Arijit Kundu

item.title: A Fractional Chern Semimetal: Exact Wavefunction and Conformal Criticality
item.description: arXiv:2611.31234v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Unlike fractional quantum Hall states in uniform Landau levels, fractional Chern insulators can host dispersive anyon bands, raising the question of what happens when the anyon gap closes. We construct an exact finite-bond-dimension tensor-network state for a fractional Chern semimetal by Gutzwiller projecting a critical parton state. This state exhibits divergent correlation lengths in charged sectors but a fractionally quantized many-body Chern number of $1/3$. Although it has one electron per unit cell, its modular $S$ and $T$ matrices and entanglement spectrum match those of the $\nu=1/3$ Laughlin state. We identify a $(1+1)$--dimensional $U(3)_1\times SU(3)_1$ conformal field theory (CFT) governing the wavefunction norm in the infrared, an unexpected result for a state with $U(1)_3$ topology. The $SU(3)_1$ sector is a nonlinear sigma model whose Wess--Zumino level and kinetic stiffness are determined by the parton Chern number and Fubini--Study metric, respectively. Under renormalization, it flows to the conformal fixed point, with an initial distance to this fixed point controlled by the idealness of parton quantum geometry. Favorable geometry enables precise agreement with CFT predictions even on narrow cylinders.
item.dc:creator: Fa-Jie Wang, Yang Qi, Zhi-Da Song

item.title: Quantum-geometry-tuned Mott transition and emergent heavy fermions in a topological flat band
item.description: arXiv:2611.31242v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A flat band with a nonzero Chern number has no localized Wannier orbitals, which raises the question of whether Mott physics is still possible. We place a Hubbard interaction $U$ on coherent orbitals, which are localized but overcomplete, and develop a single-site dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for this model. Within the flat band alone, DMFT reproduces the experimentally observed cascade and inverse-compressibility sawtooth without invoking Dirac revival or remote-band electrons. At nonzero integer filling we find an insulator-to-metal transition tuned by $s^2$, the fraction of the Brillouin zone that carries the Berry curvature. For $N_f=8$ flavors the Mott transition at $\nu=-2$ occurs at $s^2_c\approx0.025$, where the top of the lower Hubbard band reaches the Fermi level and the local moments are Kondo screened, forming a heavy Fermi liquid (HFL). The HFL extends to the hole-doped side, $\nu=-2-x$, but above the small Kondo temperature $T_K$ the state is an incoherent bad metal without a Fermi surface. At low temperature, an anti-Hund's coupling $J_A\sim0.1U$ replaces the HFL with a pseudogap metal that has a small Fermi surface and is dominated by spin-polaron excitations at small $x$. We propose this pseudogap metal as the parent state of superconductivity in TBG. The framework may also be applied to other topological bands, such as those of twisted WSe$_2$.
item.dc:creator: Ya-Hui Zhang

item.title: Direct electron cooling at millikelvin temperatures with quantum-well heat pump
item.description: arXiv:2207.14237v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Unconventional solid-state cooling is proposed whereby the electron subband degeneracy of a semiconductor quantum well is cycled at cryogenic temperatures. By "expanding" electrons to higher subband degeneracy and "compressing" to lower degeneracy in an Otto cycle, a stack of ultra-wide 150 nm GaAs quantum wells filling a 1 cm3 volume could be operated as a heat pump to pump 26 uW at 100 mK. Operated as a refrigerator, it can piggy-back onto dilution refrigerators to cool from T_base to T_base/4. Possible cooling applications include quantum computers and infrared detectors.
item.dc:creator: Chulin Wang, Thomas Douglas, Matthew A Grayson

item.title: Transport of Dirac magnons driven by gauge fields
item.description: arXiv:2512.13362v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a unified quantum field theory for Dirac magnons coupled to emergent gauge fields. At zero temperature, any space- and time-dependent gauge perturbation drives magnons out of equilibrium, generating spin currents and magnon accumulation without conventional thermal or chemical potential gradients. For a honeycomb ferromagnet, we derive closed-form expressions for the induced density and current. In the DC limit, the transverse spin conductivity quantizes to $\sigma^{xy}=\alpha^2\text{sgn}(m)\hbar/4\pi$, a magnonic analog of the quantum Hall effect, where $m$ is the topological magnon mass and $\alpha$ a dimensionless coupling constant. In the AC regime, the conductivity exhibits a sharp resonance when the drive frequency matches the topological gap $\Delta$, signaling interband transitions. Our work establishes gauge fields as a versatile tool for controlling magnon transport and reveals topologically protected quantized responses.
item.dc:creator: Luis Fern\'andez, Ka Shen, Leandro O. Nascimento, Van S\'ergio Alves, Roberto E. Troncoso, Nicolas Vidal-Silva

item.title: Characterizing electronic scattering rates with transport in multiterminal devices
item.description: arXiv:2605.03030v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Strongly interacting electrons in clean two-dimensional devices are theorized to exhibit many distinct transport regimes, such as ballistic, hydrodynamic, or diffusive. Realistic samples often lie in crossover regimes between these idealized limits. We show how a single experiment on a multiterminal device can distinguish these regimes and constrain the relevant scattering rates without space-resolved imaging. Using a linearized Boltzmann model in a five-terminal geometry, we find that current partition among the drain contacts diagnoses the ballistic-hydrodynamic-Ohmic crossover and allows extraction of momentum-relaxing and momentum-conserving scattering rates in the crossover regime. The same geometry also exhibits clear signatures of the tomographic regime, potentially allowing for a quantitative discrimination between viscous and tomographic flow in experiments. Our results demonstrate that multiterminal devices are a simpler experimental route to characterize transport regimes in electron liquids, relative to space-resolved imaging experiments.
item.dc:creator: Jack H. Farrell, Andrew Lucas

item.title: Symmetry-Protected Bipartite Entanglement in Hopf-Linked Quantum Rings
item.description: arXiv:2605.26622v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study two interacting electrons in Hopf-linked quantum rings, one electron on each ring. In the absence of the inter-ring interaction, the two lowest orbital states on each ring have the same energy. For the ideal geometry, the Fourier coefficients of the three-dimensional Coulomb kernel satisfy $V_{1,0}=-V_{0,1}$, making the positive-parity block of the four-state Hamiltonian diagonal in the Bell basis. Unitary symmetries of the full orbital Hamiltonian preserve the parity sectors under virtual transitions. For pure states odd under ring exchange followed by a half-turn on each ring ($\mathcal Y=-1$), the Schmidt weights occur in equal pairs, giving at least one bit of entanglement between the rings. An elliptic deformation changes the Coulomb selection rule to first order while preserving the link. Finite-basis diagonalization shows that higher orbitals can reduce the probability of obtaining the encoded Bell pair by projection onto the two lowest orbitals of each ring even when the entanglement between the rings remains close to one bit.
item.dc:creator: V. Yogesh, Prosenjit Maity

item.title: Quantum transport in Cooper pair splitters using hierarchical equations of motion
item.description: arXiv:2607.22235v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate charge transport in Cooper pair splitters beyond the weak-coupling and Markovian limits. To this end, we employ hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM), which can capture the combined effects of strong coupling to the leads, nonperturbative interactions, and finite voltage and temperature differences. Within this framework, we compute the electric currents as functions of the level positions of a Cooper pair splitter for various voltage and temperature configurations. In the large-bias regime, our results reduce to analytical expressions obtained from a Markovian Lindblad equation. However, recent experiments were conducted with finite voltage or temperature differences, where a Markovian description may not suffice. In this regime, HEOM yield quantitative agreement with the measured currents. We can also account for an experimentally observed thermoelectric effect in Cooper pair splitters. Our results show that HEOM provide a useful framework for describing nonequilibrium quantum transport in Cooper pair splitters and related hybrid devices.
item.dc:creator: Riya Baruah, Neill Lambert, Franco Nori, Christian Flindt

item.title: Topological Charge-Transfer Excitons
item.description: arXiv:2608.05308v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Excitons possess internal structure absent from single-particle Bloch particles, allowing their band topology to emerge from the bound-state structure rather than being inherited from their constituents. This raises the question of how the internal structure of a bound state can provide a microscopic origin of exciton topology. Here we show that the real-space embedding of charge-transfer excitons can generate an intrinsic manifold of symmetry-related off-site composite orbitals whose coupling supports topological exciton bands. Lateral electron-hole separation embeds the localized exciton on the bond connecting its constituent sites rather than on either site. We demonstrate this mechanism in a honeycomb lattice, where three bond-centered charge-transfer exciton orbitals form a Kagome lattice. By solving the Bethe-Salpeter equation, we show that this emergent multi-orbital manifold supports a topological exciton flat band upon time-reversal symmetry breaking, even when the electron and hole bands are topologically trivial. The resulting band exhibits nearly uniformly distributed quantum geometry, favorable for interaction-driven bosonic states. Our results establish a general route toward topological bands of localized composite bound states and unconventional strongly correlated bosonic phases.
item.dc:creator: Huiyuan Zheng, Kaijie Yang, Ting Cao, Di Xiao

item.title: Axion electrodynamics and the advection-diffusion structure of TEM modes in hollow-conductor waveguides
item.description: arXiv:2611.22839v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a systematic investigation of transverse electromagnetic (TEM) modes in hollow-conductor waveguides filled with a dielectric medium described by axion electrodynamics. While such modes do not propagate in conventional single-conductor waveguides, the coupling of the axion field to an external magnetic field enables their propagation. We show that the resulting TEM modes are governed by an advection-diffusion-type equation for the transverse electrostatic potential, establishing a direct mathematical connection between axion electrodynamics and advection-diffusion phenomena. We illustrate this connection through explicit solutions and field profiles for cylindrical waveguides, considering uniform and rigid rotational drift fields, both individually and in combination, as well as different values of the parameter controlling the advection-to-diffusion ratio (P\'eclet number). These results establish a transport-based framework for understanding how spatial variations of the axion-electrodynamics background shape the transverse electromagnetic fields in hollow-conductor waveguides.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'e H. Gomes

item.title: Probing Fractional Quantum Hall states in weakly interacting Fermi gases
item.description: arXiv:2509.22606v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum gases are used to simulate the physics of the lowest Landau level with neutral atoms, which in the simplest setup is achieved by rotating the gas at the confining harmonic trap frequency, a requirement that is difficult to meet in practice. However, it is known that lowest Landau level states appear among the excited states of weakly interacting gases, even in a nonrotating trap, by working at fixed finite angular momentum. Thus, even in the absence of rotations or for moderate rotation frequencies, fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states can be accessed as excited states at finite angular momentum. Motivated by this, and by recent experimentally demonstrated excitation protocols for two particles, we show that such states can be selectively addressed at larger particle numbers, and we propose imaging techniques to resolve their distinct microscopic structure. In particular, we suggest that recently developed excitation and imaging techniques for rotating few-fermion systems allow for a detailed experimental investigation of FQH wave functions and of the crossover to large particle numbers. We illustrate the evolution of the excitation spectrum with rotations at weak interactions for $N=6$ spin-balanced fermions and show how sampling of the few-body wave function allows one to discriminate between total guiding-center, center-of-mass vortex, and hyperradial excitations, thus providing detailed and versatile probes of the microscopic structure of FQH states.
item.dc:creator: Viktor Bekassy, Mikael Fogelstr\"om, Johannes Hofmann

item.title: Gradually opening Schr\"odinger's box reveals a cascade of sharp dynamical transitions
item.description: arXiv:2602.02672v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum mechanics predicts that unobserved systems may exist in a superposition of states, yet measurement produces definite outcomes, a tension at the heart of the quantum-to-classical boundary. How the transformation between these opposing regimes unfolds as observation strength increases has remained experimentally elusive. Here, by continuously tuning the measurement strength on a superconducting qubit, we reveal that measurement-dominated dynamics emerge not gradually but through multiple sharp transitions marked by the halting of coherent oscillations, state freezing near an attracting state, and the onset of quantum Zeno dynamics. Decoherence, rather than washing out this structure, reshapes it, reordering the transitions and decoupling signatures that coincide in idealised models. These results establish that the passage from quantum dynamics to measurement-dominated behaviour unfolds through a sequence of distinct transitions governed by the interplay between observation and environment.
item.dc:creator: Barkay Guttel, Danielle Gov, Noam Netzer, Uri Goldblatt, Sergey Hazanov, Lalit M. Joshi, Alessandro Romito, Yuval Gefen, Parveen Kumar, Kyrylo Snizhko, Fabien Lafont, Serge Rosenblum

item.title: Fluctuation imaging of disorder in monolayer semiconductors
item.description: arXiv:2603.07418v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Monolayer semiconductors hold great potential for nanoscale electronics, optoelectronics, and photonics. Excitons dominate their optical properties. As their electric fields extend outside the monolayer, they are sensitive to their surroundings. Thus, disorder can cause exciton instability, which is detrimental to device performance and critical for scalability and reproducibility. Here, we adapt a super-resolution fluorescence fluctuation microscopy technique to image localized exciton fluctuations in monolayer semiconductors, allowing us to identify unstable spots in an otherwise continuous monolayer with constant fluorescence. These spots correspond to interfacial disorder measured by atomic force microscopy. We examine how different material interfaces influence the fluctuations by comparing several substrates and provide additional insight into the disorder behind the fluctuations using hyperspectral imaging. We also assess the reduction of disorder upon thermal annealing, evidenced by a decrease in fluctuations. Our results show that fluorescence fluctuation imaging can detect disorder features similar to those of atomic force microscopy and hyperspectral imaging, while being faster and easier to implement. Therefore, it is a promising method for evaluating the quality of monolayer semiconductors, particularly when integrated with nanostructures and heterostructures found in nano-optoelectronic devices.
item.dc:creator: Tom T. C. Sistermans, Rasmus H. Godiksen, Sara A. Elrafei, Alberto G. Curto

item.title: High-Power Laser Drives Motion in Ultra-thin Photonic Crystal Lightsails
item.description: arXiv:2606.20149v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Laser-driven lightsails require reflectors that are ultralight, highly reflective and robust under intense illumination. These demands point to the thinnest reflectors that dielectric optics allows, photonic crystals, in which a perforated membrane thinner than the wavelength of light acts as a mirror. Such mirrors reflect by confining light inside the membrane, but this confinement also amplifies absorption, making ultralow-loss, tension-bearing materials essential. Stoichiometric high-stress silicon nitride uniquely meets both requirements, yet its ~1 GPa stress makes large, compliant structures difficult to release intact, and such sails have never been pushed by high-power lasers. Here we demonstrate millimeter-wide, 200-nm-thick photonic-crystal trampolines in this material, with 99% design reflectivity at 1070 nm and a static stiffness of 0.53 N/m. Radiation pressure displaces them by more than a micrometer within 50 microseconds. In air, they withstand several times the irradiance found at the Sun's surface, delivered as a coherent beam. Light reshapes the sail more than it pushes it, since modest temperature differences buckle the membrane and collapse its stiffness, so thermal deformation outpaces radiation pressure within milliseconds. The interaction and compliance that make lightsails movable also let light deform them. These results establish a testbed for high-power nanophotonics, directed-energy systems and light-driven propulsion.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Norder, Ata Ke\c{s}kekler, Richard A. Norte

item.title: Micromotion and topological constraints on Floquet-state quantum geometry
item.description: arXiv:2608.13649v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The quantum geometry of Floquet-Bloch states in periodically driven crystals evolves throughout each drive cycle. We show that Floquet topology and micromotion constrain this evolution. Using a projector formulation that separates stroboscopic and micromotion contributions, we bound the deviation of the integrated quantum metric of any Floquet-band subspace from its stroboscopic value and derive a geometric speed limit on its evolution. In chiral Floquet systems, these bounds extend the topological lower bounds set by the $0$- and $\pi$-gap invariants at two symmetry-selected times into finite intervals of the drive, a dynamical topological obstruction. When both invariants are nonzero, it can force a minimum intra-period change in the metric, driven by micromotion. Because the integrated metric is a periodic lower bound on the total spread of time-evolved Wannier functions, such a change can make this spread breathe. An exactly solvable driven spin chain realizes this obstruction and further hosts a flat-band point where each band's metric equals the breathing of its compact localized state. This equality provides a direct geometric characterization of local micromotion, accessible through local spin correlators.
item.dc:creator: Arpit Raj, Johannes Mitscherling, Bj\"orn Trauzettel

item.title: Singlet-triplet superconductivity from repulsive interactions in a $p$-wave magnet
item.description: arXiv:2611.14609v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by recent proposals of $p$-wave magnets, which host odd-parity spin splitting, we study electrons near Van Hove singularities with local repulsive interactions. We demonstrate how the symmetry of the $p$-wave spin splitting governs the competition among instabilities. Using a parquet renormalization group (pRG) analysis of a simple one-sublattice model of a $p$-wave magnet, we find that superconductivity is the leading instability over the entire phase diagram for purely repulsive interactions. The resulting superconducting state is generically a mixture of spin-singlet and spin-triplet pairing and approaches an equal-weight mixture when $T_c$ is small compared with the energy offset between each Van Hove electron and its inversion partner. Extending the pRG analysis to a more realistic two-sublattice model, we find that superconductivity remains the leading instability, while the sublattice degree of freedom leads to a competition among various singlet-triplet pairing channels and even a finite-momentum equal-spin pair-density wave. Our mechanism applies broadly to odd-parity magnets and opens a natural route to nodal topological superconductivity.
item.dc:creator: Hanbit Oh, Laura Classen, Daniel F. Agterberg
